- Added support in TestAccessor to resolve compiler-generated backing fields for auto-implemented properties.
- Added a new helper method GetAutoPropertyBackingField() that searches for fields named <PropertyName>k__BackingField.
- Updated member lookup logic to attempt auto-property backing field resolution when a field is not found.
- Added unit tests for reading, writing, read-only, and inherited auto-properties.

Issues.Title: release-notes in .NET 11 Rc 1
Issues.Body:
## Overall summary

- **Total qualifying PRs:** 19 merged PRs in milestone `11.0-rc1`.
- **Main feature areas:** Kiosk mode and .NET 11 APIs; modern visual styles and dark mode; ComboBox rendering; control reliability; DPI, right-to-left, and designer behavior; documentation and localization.
- **Key fixes worth highlighting:** the new `KioskModeManager`, restored Clipboard text conversion behavior, dark-mode consistency, several .NET 11 ComboBox rendering corrections, the PrintPreviewControl black-page regression, TaskDialog crash prevention, and PictureBox handle-race mitigation.
- **Release Notes recommendation:** Include 16 user-facing feature, compatibility, rendering, and reliability fixes. Omit three documentation, localization, or designer-metadata-only items from the main narrative. The search returned 30 merged PRs; nine automated source-update PRs plus PRs #14809 and #14767, whose changes were already delivered in Preview 7, were excluded before this report.

## Features and API surface

| PR | Fixed Contents | Description | Comment |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| [#14892](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14892) | `System.Windows.Forms.KioskModeManager` | Adds a designer-friendly kiosk-mode component with full-screen restoration, optional topmost behavior, keyboard and Escape handling, pointer auto-hide, power-saving suppression, and support for components hosted by forms or user controls. It also removes the unshipped `TreeView.NodeLeading` API while retaining TreeView update integration. | **Include and highlight.** This is a substantial new .NET 11 capability and an RC1 API-surface decision. |

## Clipboard, printing, and reliability

| PR | Fixed Contents | Description | Comment |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| [#14893](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14893) | `System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard` | Restores the pre-.NET 10 `autoConvert` behavior for typed Clipboard APIs, preventing Unicode text from being returned as mojibake by `GetText` and related paths. | **Include and highlight.** This fixes a customer-visible Clipboard data-corruption regression. |
| [#14857](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14857) | `System.Windows.Forms.PrintPreviewControl` | Uses a white preview-page background when `ForeColor` has not been explicitly set, while preserving an explicitly configured color. This prevents empty `PrintDocument` previews from appearing black. | **Include.** This is a clear regression fix with visible impact. |
| [#14842](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14842) | `System.Windows.Forms.TaskDialogPage` | Adds bounds checks when mapping native custom-button and radio-button IDs, and safely handles unmatched IDs instead of throwing `IndexOutOfRangeException`. | **Include.** It prevents an application crash on unexpected native TaskDialog results. |
| [#14826](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14826) | `System.Windows.Forms.PictureBox` | Checks `IsHandleCreated` before `InvokeRequired` in animated-image frame callbacks, avoiding a handle creation/destruction race that could produce “Error creating window handle.” | **Include.** This addresses an intermittent runtime reliability failure. |

## Modern visual styles, dark mode, and rendering

| PR | Fixed Contents | Description | Comment |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| [#14889](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14889) | `System.Windows.Forms.TreeView` and `ListView` tooltips | Applies the native dark Explorer theme to mouse-hover tooltip windows when dark mode is enabled, matching the controls and their keyboard tooltips. | **Include.** This is a visible dark-mode consistency fix. |
| [#14888](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14888) | `System.Windows.Forms.ErrorProvider` tooltip | Applies dark-mode theming to the ErrorProvider native tooltip while preserving high-contrast and non-dark behavior. | **Include.** It improves readability and visual consistency in dark-mode applications. |
| [#14874](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14874) | `System.Windows.Forms.ComboBox` text layout | Preserves the native single-line edit-child height in `VisualStylesMode.Net11`, preventing text clipping in editable DropDown and Simple ComboBoxes. | **Include.** This fixes a prominent .NET 11 rendering defect. |
| [#14861](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14861) | `System.Windows.Forms.ComboBox` drop-down button | Stops the .NET 11 renderer from deriving the drop-down button surface from `BackColor`, so custom background colors affect only the editable field and the button retains system chrome. | **Include.** This restores expected `BackColor` behavior in modern visual styles. |
| [#14852](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14852) | `System.Windows.Forms.ComboBox.FlatStyle` | Recreates or relays out the native handle when switching between modern rendering and `FlatStyle.System`, eliminating stale button geometry and designer artifacts. | **Include.** It fixes both design-time and runtime visual-style transitions. |
| [#14843](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14843) | Disabled `System.Windows.Forms.ComboBox` rendering | Uses a shared, dark-mode- and high-contrast-aware system disabled palette and handles the native edit child consistently, rather than muting custom colors or leaving a white field. | **Include.** This makes disabled state rendering recognizable and consistent. |
| [#14833](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14833) | `System.Windows.Forms.ControlPaint.Light` | Performs HLS color interpolation with integer arithmetic and delays the byte cast, producing correct lightened values for system colors such as `SystemColors.Control`. | **Include.** It corrects a public rendering helper and may affect custom control painting. |
| [#14813](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14813) | `CheckBox` and `RadioButton` toggle-switch rendering | Routes transparent and image-backed toggle-switch backgrounds through normal WinForms background painting while retaining a fast path for opaque colors, removing black-background artifacts during animation. | **Include.** This is a visible fix for the new toggle-switch appearance. |
| [#14742](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14742) | `System.Windows.Forms.Form` dark title bar | Reapplies the immersive dark-mode DWM attribute when a top-level form handle is recreated, preserving a dark title bar after changing `RightToLeft` or `ShowInTaskbar`. | **Include.** It fixes a conspicuous dark-mode mismatch in common handle-recreation scenarios. |

## DPI, right-to-left, and designer behavior

| PR | Fixed Contents | Description | Comment |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| [#14828](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14828) | `System.Windows.Forms.PropertyGrid` toolbar | Recomputes toolbar image scaling, margins, and button DPI from the current monitor when rebuilding the toolbar, fixing oversized or poorly scaled icons after PerMonitorV2 DPI changes. | **Include.** This is a long-standing multi-monitor DPI usability fix. |
| [#14820](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14820) | Multiline `System.Windows.Forms.TextBox` scrollbar | Accounts for `WS_EX_LEFTSCROLLBAR` at runtime and `RightToLeft` before handle creation, reserving padding on the correct side so the vertical scrollbar remains visible. | **Include.** This is a user-visible RTL layout correction. |
| [#14814](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14814) | `PropertyGrid.VisualStylesModeChanged` | Hides the event from the designer Events window to match the already hidden `VisualStylesMode` property. | **Omit from main Release Notes.** Correct but too narrow and design-time-only for the primary customer-facing list. |

## Documentation and localization

| PR | Fixed Contents | Description | Comment |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| [#14880](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14880) | `CheckBox.CheckAlign` and `RadioButton.CheckAlign` documentation | Documents that toggle-switch appearances treat left and center alignment values as left-aligned, and right values as right-aligned, rather than centering the switch. | **Omit from main Release Notes.** This clarifies existing intended behavior without changing runtime behavior. |
| [#14818](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14818) | `System.Windows.Forms` localized resources | Checks translated resource files generated by the OneLocBuild localization pipeline into the repository. | **Omit from main Release Notes.** This is automated localization maintenance rather than a discrete feature or fix. |

Issues.Title: Restoring autoConvert behavior in Clipboard APIs
Issues.Body:
Fixes mojibake character issue in https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/issues/14322

## Description

Till .NET 9.0, `autoConvert` was set to true only for `FileDrop` and `Bitmap` scenarios. However, since .NET 10, it is being set to true for `GetAudioStream`, `GetFileDropList`, `GetImage`, and `GetText` APIs inside the private method `GetTypedDataIfAvailable`. This causes issues with GetText API with mojibake characters as described in the bug.

## Customer Impact

There is no way for the app to know whether the clipboard contents were corrupted or if there is any problem with the API as it didn't get the desired data.

## Regression

Yes - from .NET 9.0

## Testing

Created a WinForms app to write unicode data on the clipboard and another app to read it. Before the changes, the reader app returned several hits for mojibake characters. After fix, there were none.

## Risk

This should be a very low risk change as this behavior was working fine in 9.0 and previous versions.

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Common package omits required System.Formats.Nrbf dependency
Issues.Body:
### Description

`System.Drawing.Common` version `11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103` ships `lib/net11.0/System.Private.Windows.Core.dll`, which has a direct assembly reference to `System.Formats.Nrbf, Version=11.0.0.0`. However, the package's `net11.0` nuspec dependency group declares only `Microsoft.Win32.SystemEvents`.

As a result, NuGet restore does not resolve `System.Formats.Nrbf`, and publish does not copy `System.Formats.Nrbf.dll` or include it in the ReadyToRun compiler reference closure. This produces an invalid deployment closure.

### Reproduction

1. Restore or publish an application that references `System.Drawing.Common` `11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103` for `net11.0`.
2. Inspect `project.assets.json`: the `System.Drawing.Common` target entry lists these runtime assets:
   - `System.Drawing.Common.dll`
   - `System.Private.Windows.Core.dll`
   - `System.Private.Windows.GdiPlus.dll`
3. The same entry contains only this dependency:
   - `Microsoft.Win32.SystemEvents`
4. `System.Formats.Nrbf` has no resolved node and is not copied to publish output.
5. ReadyToRun/Crossgen2 fails while processing `System.Private.Windows.Core.dll`:

```
Error: Failed to load assembly 'System.Formats.Nrbf'
Internal.TypeSystem.TypeSystemException+FileNotFoundException: Failed to load assembly 'System.Formats.Nrbf'
```

Adding the matching `System.Formats.Nrbf.dll` to the Crossgen2 reference set makes the same compilation complete successfully.

### Source cause

`System.Private.Windows.Core.csproj` references `System.Formats.Nrbf`. `System.Drawing.Common.csproj` packs `System.Private.Windows.Core` using a project reference with `Pack=true` and `PrivateAssets=all`, which embeds the assembly but suppresses its NuGet dependency edge from the resulting `System.Drawing.Common` package.

### Expected behavior

The `net11.0` `System.Drawing.Common` package dependency group should make `System.Formats.Nrbf` available to consumers, so publish and ReadyToRun receive a complete runtime assembly closure.

### Suggested fix

Add a `System.Formats.Nrbf` package dependency to `System.Drawing.Common` for the applicable target frameworks, or otherwise change the package authoring so the dependency of the packed `System.Private.Windows.Core` asset is propagated.

### Additional context

This was observed while investigating https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/132225. The same missing manifest edge appears in `11.0.0-preview.6.26359.118`; .NET 11 preview 7 Crossgen2 exposes it during ReadyToRun compilation.

Issues.Title: Improve Net11 TextBox text layout by reducing excess vertical whitespace
Issues.Body: ## Root Cause Under the Net11 modern style, inconsistencies have arisen in the calculations regarding the "external height contract" and the "internal available client area" for TextBox, ComboBox, and UpDown controls. On one hand, they retain the height semantics of classic single-line edit controls (Everett); on the other, they introduce a more aggressive modern "chrome/padding carve." This combination leads to two types of issues in scenarios involving small heights, `AutoSize` settings, or DPI/text scaling: 1. The client height is excessively compressed (risking text visibility); 2. Alternatively, visual whitespace is increased to avoid compression (inconsistent with height expectations for classic controls). ## Proposed changes - TextBoxBase: Reverted `PreferredHeightCore` to the classic formula (maintaining compatibility with existing contracts); added a minimum single-line client height safeguard for the modern padding "carve" within `WM_NCCALCSIZE`, and implemented tiered compression of the top/bottom carve based on border visibility to prevent the text area from being crushed. - ComboBox (Modern): Aligned the preferred height in modern mode with the classic height; adjusted the modern chrome inset to "preserve horizontal spacing while minimizing vertical spacing," thereby reducing excess vertical whitespace while maintaining text readability. - UpDownBase: Introduced a constant for modern button width (14 logical units) and applied it to the button group width; added adaptive vertical carve compression to the modern layout (while preserving a minimum visible border strip); implemented extended top/bottom border rendering to improve the continuity of rounded borders. - ModernControlVisualStyles: Standardized and reduced the relevant corner radii (for Field and UpDown controls) to align with the new geometric and border visual style. - Tests: Performed a batch update and added new tests covering classic height contracts, `AutoSize`/layout stability, minimum text measurement safeguards in DPI scenarios, and padding boundaries versus border visibility. ## Customer Impact - Single-line input controls using the modern style are more stable across different DPI and text scaling settings: they are less prone to text clipping or unexpected increases in height and whitespace. - Layouts that rely on preferred height—such as `TableLayoutPanel`—behave more predictably, with fewer visual jumps. - Compatibility with legacy WinForms height behavior is maintained, reducing the risk of regressions when upgrading existing applications to the new style. ## Screenshots ### Before ### After **Scale 350%** **Scale 300%** **Scale 225%** **Scale 150%** **Scale 100%** **Screen recording** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a42f810b-df77-4289-a47f-0be5e676581a ## Test methodology - Manually - Automated test cases ## Test environment(s) - 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14887)

Issues.Title: Fix Issue 14793: ToolStripTextBox renders incorrectly when hosted in MenuStrip
Issues.Body: Fixes #14793 ## Root Cause When a `ToolStripControlHost` hosts a control (such as a `ToolStripTextBox` or `ToolStripComboBox`), the control's own `VisualStylesMode` can still utilize the .NET 11 modern rendering path; however, the rendering models for the non-client areas and borders of the `ToolStrip`/`MenuStrip` (especially when not using the System renderer) do not align with those of the hosted control. This results in rendering pipeline incompatibilities, leading to artifacts such as light-colored blocks or incorrectly drawn borders. ## Proposed changes - Added a policy within ToolStripControlHost: - Once a control is hosted in a ToolStrip or MenuStrip, if its VisualStylesMode is set to a modern mode (such as Net11, Latest, or Inherit), it is forced to Classic mode. - If the control is set to Net11 while in the hosted state, it is immediately reverted to Classic. - The original requested value is restored after the control is removed from the host (to avoid permanently altering the control's state). - Comments for Control.VisualStylesMode and VisualStylesMode.Net11 explicitly state that this mode does not apply to ToolStripControlHost scenarios. - Added unit tests (in ToolStripControlHostTests) to provide coverage: ## Customer Impact When using Dark Mode with `VisualStylesMode=Net11`, applications utilizing `ToolStripControlHost` exhibit noticeable UI flaws—such as anomalous borders or backgrounds—that compromise interface consistency and a professional appearance. While functionality generally remains intact, visual quality suffers, and the issue is more easily reproduced under `Professional` or `ManagerRenderMode`. For menus or toolbars relying on `ToolStripTextBox` or `ToolStripComboBox`, this is a highly visible issue that directly impacts the end-user experience. ## Regression? - No ## Risk - Mini ## Screenshots ### Before ### After ## Test methodology - Manually - Automated test cases ## Test environment(s) - 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14873)
